Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC task-c4b91aa4: replicate a template across divider panels

Use when a grid is partitioned by complete straight divider lines (often color 6) into congruent rectangular panels, one panel contains a colored pattern, and the other panels are mostly a uniform blank/background (observed as 1). Copy the template panel's contents into each corresponding panel, preserving the divider lines.

## Validated behavior
- Demo: 5×9 input with a full vertical divider column of 3 at column 4. The 5×4 panel to the left was uniform 7 (blank), while the right 5×4 panel held a pattern. Output copied the right pattern into the left panel, preserving the divider. Pattern pixels were copied exactly, including its 7-valued cells; this is panel replication rather than recoloring.
- Fresh test: 11×13 input with full horizontal divider row 3 and full vertical divider column 6 (both color 6), forming four 3×6 panels with 3×6 content spans. The top-left panel contained a 3×6 template; remaining panels were blank 1s. Output tiled the exact 3×6 template into all four panels, preserving both divider lines. Accepted.

## Additional accepted fresh test
- A 17×11 grid had divider rows 5 and 11 and divider columns 3 and 7, all color 4, producing nine congruent 5×3 panels. The top-left panel contained a sparse pattern (7s and a 9) on background 1; the other eight panels were blank 1. The accepted output repeated the top-left panel's complete 5×3 contents into every panel, preserving all divider rows/columns. This confirms tiling across a 3×3 panel layout, not just a single split or a 2×2 layout.

## Additional accepted fresh test
- A 17×29 grid had divider row 8 and divider columns 9 and 19, all color 3, yielding six congruent 8×9 panels (3 columns × 2 rows). The top-left panel contained a sparse template on background 1, including a 7 at its top-left, another 7, and a 0; all remaining panels were blank 1s. The accepted output tiled the entire top-left 8×9 panel across all six positions, preserving the divider lines. This confirms a 3×2 panel layout and exact copying of all template cells.

## Procedure
1. Find complete divider rows/columns and treat them as immutable boundaries.
2. Identify congruent panel dimensions and locate the populated template panel.
3. Repeat the template panel's entire cell matrix into every other aligned panel, including template-colored/background cells; do not merely stamp non-background marks or recolor the blanks.
4. Preserve divider cells and validate dimensions and panel alignment before submitting.

## Additional accepted fresh test
- A 13×15 grid had a full horizontal divider row 6 and vertical divider column 7, both color 6, making four 6×7 panels. The top-left panel was a pattern of 5s on background 7; the other three panels were entirely 7. The accepted output copied the complete top-left 6×7 panel into all four positions, preserving both dividers. This confirms exact template tiling when the blank-panel background matches the template background, too.

Do not assume this rule for arbitrary grids without the full-divider/congruent-panel structure. The top-left pattern features three 3's as background and two marks, while other panels seem blank. So, I’ll replicate the top-left content across each panel while making sure the dividers are preserved. I'll construct each row to ensure the correct pattern is repeated across the grid.

**Designing panel output**

I'm looking to ensure every panel shares the same pattern and that row separators are at every 8. For the output, row 1 will have the pattern P 8 P 8 P, and I'll replicate this for row 2 as well. This pattern continues, with row 7 filled entirely with 8s. The same design needs to repeat for the six lower rows. I need to format everything as a precise JSON action to maintain consistency across the grid.
